newsitem.title: USA: UAW sets GM truck plant strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: UAW sets GM truck plant strike deadline.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Tuesday the United Auto Workers has set a strike deadline for 11:59 p.m. (EDT) April 22 for contract talks at the company's Pontiac East pickup truck assembly plant in Pontiac, Mich.

GM received the "five-day" notification from the UAW on Tuesday. The notification means that if a new labor contract is not reached by the deadline, the union has the option of striking or continuing negotiations.
"Management and local union officials continue to talk and we remain hopeful an agreement can be reached without a work stoppage," said GM spokesman Daniel Flores.

About 4,100 members of UAW Local 594 work at the plant, which runs three shifts. The facility produces full-size regular cab and extended cab GMC and Chevrolet C/K pickup trucks, as well as chassis cab trucks.
Another 1,300 hourly UAW employees work in an engineering unit that makes prototype products.
UAW officials said the two sides have been unable to agree on a variety of manpower issues, such as work GM wants to subcontract, and line-speed accelerations.

GM continues to negotiate with UAW bargainers at Local 1999 in Oklahoma City, Okla. About 3,500 hourly workers struck the company's car plant in there April 4 when contract talks broke down. The plant makes the redesigned Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass sedans.
